chapter: Swing, singers, Ed Fox and recordings
title: The band book and the 1936 accident that broke his bass
summary: Trunk fell and broke the neck, repaired in Galveston.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: How long would a tune stay in the books?
Oh, my goodness, the edges would be --
Oh, my goodness, it was at least about three or four inches thick.

Yeah, well, we had to have the regular bookcase made up to put the music in. Put them in there, you just opened up where you could get to them, you know. Then when your valet would pack up at night, they'd take them and put them in a long thing like this.
Two of them they had, oblong. One of those is the one that snapped the neck on my fiddle when we had that accident. Shifted to the --
Yeah. Shifted to the back. Fell on the neck and broke the neck.
Second accident. And you went on and played?
Well, we was off that night. When I got to the next town, I had -- Galveston, I found a violin maker in Galveston, repaired it. Did a dolgarn good job.
Oh, the neck of your bass?
Oh, I thought it was your neck.
